To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a novel protocol for mMTC access with integrated authentication and we have shown that the proposed protocol is more resource-efficient and achieves lower latency compared to the existing LTE protocols.
the mMTC access protocol with integrated authentication is more efficient and has lower latency than the LTE protocol family.

we have proposed and analyzed a connection establishment protocol for massive machine-type communication (MTC) with integrated authentication and that the proposed solution achieves a lower latency for Poisson arrivals, lower signalling overhead, and higher resource utilization compared to the existing solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental problem of the 5G and beyond systems, namely the connection establishment/access with integrated security.
the following question: Can we use authentication and encryption algorithms in the connection establishment/access phase, and if yes, what are the advantages of doing so?
the design of a new access protocol that integrates authentication into the connection establishment process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integration of security features, such as authentication, in access protocols, is a promising direction for mMTC.

the mMTC connection establishment protocol with the integrated security features proposed in this paper outperforms the LTE-based connection establishment protocol in terms of latency, signalling overhead and system resources utilization.

our protocol is more efficient than the LTE protocol family and the LTE-A Pro protocol in terms of latency and signalling overhead, and it is as efficient as the LTE-A Pro in terms of energy consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mMTC access can benefit from the integration of security features in the access protocols.
we present an efficient protocol for mMTC access with integrated authentication and that it is based on a new signature scheme, that is inspired by the MILENAGES algorithm.
we have shown that it is possible to integrate authentication into the mMTC connection establishment/access protocols and that this integration is beneficial for mMTC traffic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mMCTC traffic benefits profoundly from integrated security features into the access protocols.
a careful integration of security and access protocols is beneficial for mMTC.
security is not an afterthought, but a fundamental design principle for the mMTC protocols.
